The Structure of Scientific Revolutions is a 1962 book about the history of science by the philosopher Thomas S. Kuhn . Its publication was a landmark event in the history , philosophy , and sociology of science .  Kuhn challenged the then prevailing view of progress in science in which scientific progress was viewed as "development-by-accumulation" of accepted facts and theories. Kuhn argued for an episodic model in which periods of conceptual continuity and cumulative progress, referred to as periods of " normal science ", were interrupted by periods of revolutionary science. The discovery of "anomalies" accumulating and precipitating revolutions in science leads to new paradigms .  New paradigms then ask new questions of old data, move beyond the mere "puzzle-solving" [ 1 ] of the previous paradigm, alter the rules of the game and change the "map" directing new research. [ 2 ]
